creationPrompt:
Create a habit review for me as a Claw Me Page. Include notice the pattern, choose one adjustment, review without punishment. Replace illustrative data, preserve relevant evidence and uncertainty, and check totals or percentages. Ask only for missing information in one concise batch: habit, purpose, review period, observations, helpful conditions, obstacles and next adjustment.

Use the Claw Me source at https://github.com/clawdotme/plugin in templates/habit-review/index.html and templates/_shared/tailwind/README.md. Use semantic responsive HTML, working section links, and useful native details/summary interactions. No scripts, forms, tracking, or embedded frames in the static Page. Deliver matching HTML and PDF from the same content, expand disclosures for print, and inspect page breaks. Use a readable portrait PDF. Keep the result private for review; do not send messages, connect services, purchase anything, or change sharing without my instruction. PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A reflective habit review with a modest record, context, and a next-week adjustment.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional review tracks a short end-of-day planning habit. It is a personal reflection example, not medical or behavioral treatment advice.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Day: Monday · Five-minute review: Completed · Context: Started before closing laptop
Day: Tuesday · Five-minute review: Missed · Context: Late meeting
Day: Wednesday · Five-minute review: Completed · Context: Reminder beside notebook
Day: Thursday · Five-minute review: Completed · Context: Shorter version used
Day: Friday · Five-minute review: Completed · Context: Combined with weekly review
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Notice the pattern: The review happened on four of five days. The missed day followed a late meeting, while the shorter version helped on Thursday. Context is more useful here than judging the week as perfect or failed.
Choose one adjustment: Try a two-minute version on meeting-heavy days: record what moved and the next useful step. Keep the ordinary version for days with enough time.
Review without punishment: Ask whether the habit supports the work you care about. If it creates more pressure than value, change its scope or stop the experiment. The record is information, not a score of personal worth.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: journal layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
